item.title: German economy frets about Saxony-Anhalt election results
item.description: The AfD won the election in the eastern German state by a wide margin. While politicians and election analysts are still debating the reasons for the far-right party's popularity, economists are sounding the alarm.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Fifty years after Mao’s death, China has transformed. DW looks at why his political legacy still matters.
item.description: Mao Zedong was perhaps the most influential, and certainly one of the most controversial, figures in 20th-century China. Even five decades after his death, the legacy of his era continues to influence China today.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ratko Mladic’s funeral casts shadow over Bosnia and Herzegovina vote
item.description: Ratko Mladic’s funeral in Belgrade, attended by Serbian and Bosnian Serb leaders, has deepened regional tensions and could affect the upcoming election in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Japan's empty temples seek new ways to survive
item.description: With a declining population, shrinking congregations and growing economic pressures, temples are struggling to stay relevant. As more temples are sold or closed, is religion in decline in modern Japan?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: US-Canada tariff dispute weighs on cross-border ties
item.description: As Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect, Canadian and US car industries fear the trade war will hit them hard, while Canadians are cutting back on travel.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Kenya: Crackdown on foreign traders prompts xenophobia fears
item.description: Concerns about xenophobia are rising in Kenya after President William Ruto ordered a crackdown on foreigners working as hawkers. The government insists however that legally documented foreign traders remain protected.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Morocco earthquake 3 years on: 'No one has remembered us'
item.description: Morocco has rebuilt thousands of homes since the 2023 earthquake. But some survivors are still living in tents and say they have received no state aid.
item.dc:subject: Africa

item.title: Nicaragua challenges German arms exports to Israel at ICJ
item.description: Germany has asked the International Court of Justice to dismiss the case on jurisdiction grounds. It also said its arms exports to Israel were documented, published, and subject to more stringent checks than most.

item.title: War criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade, Serbia
item.description: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, has been buried in Belgrade. The funeral, broadcast live on TV, comes just days before President Vucic is expected to call an election.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Pakistan: Can creating new provinces fix governance?
item.description: Pakistanis broadly agree that the country needs more responsive and effective government, but many question whether simply creating more provinces is the solution.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Threatening letters revive fears among Kashmiri Pandits
item.description: Leaked addresses and phone numbers have reignited fears among Hindu government employees who returned to Muslim-majority Kashmir under a rehabilitation scheme.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
item.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, seeking to revive efforts to end the war. But the latest diplomatic push seems to have produced no breakthrough.
